Imperial Monetary Policies
The Ottoman Empire
Transit Policy
Allowed foreign coin
(ike Spanish reales) to
circulate uncontrolled.
Resulted in wrecked
domestic mining and
constant eastward
hemorrhage.
The Mughal Empire
Control Policy
Required land tax in
imperial coin; forced
immediate melting and
reissue of foreign silver into
rupees at ports like Surat.
Maintained monetary
sovereignty.
Tokugawa Japan
Isolation Policy
Initially leveraged mining
booms to strike large
state issues, then enforced
strict seclusion to
completely halt the export
of domestic silver by
1668.
